title: The Arrow That Tells You Which Side Your Fuel Door Is On

scenes.narration: Your car may have been answering this question your entire life.
scenes.note: Dashboard legible at frame 0. Bill mid-argument with himself about which side the tank is on.

beats.action: Bill at the wheel craning to look over both shoulders; Mina beside him, already unimpressed
a giant question mark pops over Bill's head and wobbles
the question mark multiplies into a small crowd of them; camera punch

scenes.narration: Look at the little fuel pump symbol on your dashboard.
scenes.note: Dive to the gauge. The pump icon is found before the arrow — order matters.

beats.action: camera dives into the instrument cluster; the fuel gauge fills frame
the little pump icon lights up and pulses
everything else on the cluster dims to grey so only the icon reads

scenes.narration: On many cars, there's a tiny arrow or triangle beside it.
scenes.note: The reveal beat. The arrow has to pop, not fade — it is the whole video.

beats.action: the tiny arrow pops in beside the pump icon with a hard snap and a ring of sparkles
the arrow morphs to a triangle and back, showing both forms

scenes.narration: If it points left, your fuel door is on the left. If it points right, it's on the right.
scenes.note: Top-down car so left and right are unambiguous. Two clean symmetrical demonstrations.

beats.action: hard cut to a top-down car; fuel doors drawn on both sides, both closed
the top-down car rotates a few degrees so both fuel doors stay readable
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: the arrow swings left; the LEFT fuel door flips open and glows teal
the arrow swings right; the RIGHT door opens instead and the left snaps shut

scenes.narration: Manufacturers don't all put fuel doors on the same side, so this tiny symbol saves you from guessing,
scenes.note: Why the arrow needs to exist: the industry never agreed. Show four cars disagreeing.

beats.action: the four cars shuffle order; their fuel doors still disagree
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: each car flashes its door side in turn, none of them matching
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: four little cars pop in in a row, fuel doors on alternating sides
a NO STANDARD stamp lands across the row
the arrow reappears over each car in turn, correct every time; teal ticks

scenes.narration: which means every time you pulled into a gas station, chose the wrong pump, reversed, and tried again,
scenes.note: The montage of past failure. Three beats, escalating, comic timing on the reverse.

beats.action: the arrow spins once and settles, still correct
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: Bill drives into a forecourt, confident
he stops at the wrong pump; the hose is comically far from the filler
the car reverses in a fast stepped jerk and tries again, still wrong; motion lines

scenes.narration: the answer may have been glowing directly in front of your face.
scenes.note: Return to the arrow, now glowing. Mina's non-reaction is the punchline. Hard cut.

beats.action: snap back to the dashboard; the arrow is right there
the arrow blazes gold; a spotlight cone drops onto it
pull back: it is directly in front of Bill's face; he goes deadpan; Mina slowly turns to look at him; hard cut
